## 🌍 Stellaria speaks your language

- **Twelve languages.** The theme, the Stellaria app and the setup now follow your Windows display language: English, French, Spanish, German, Brazilian Portuguese, Italian, Polish, Russian, Turkish, Simplified Chinese, Japanese and Korean. You can also pick one by hand in the theme settings (Appearance > Language) and in the app's Settings. Dates, numbers and units follow the language too.
- **A tidier tray.** The bar shows four tray icons and keeps the others behind an arrow. Turn it off in the theme settings (Desktop) if you prefer every icon.
- **Panels opened from the keyboard stay open.** The dashboard (<kbd>Win</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd>) and the utilities (<kbd>Win</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>U</kbd>) no longer close when the pointer moves away. Close them with the same shortcut, a click outside, or <kbd>Esc</kbd>.
- **The taskbar comes back exactly as it was.** Turning off "Replace the taskbar", stopping the theme or uninstalling now restores your own auto-hide setting and the screen space Windows reserves for the taskbar.
- **Fixes.** Widgets reload by themselves when their fonts fail after the PC wakes up, the welcome screen shows only once, the Stellaria app no longer stays blank after being reopened, and its Home page previews your real wallpaper, Wallpaper Engine included.

Translations other than English and French are new: if a phrase sounds wrong in your language, please [open an issue](https://github.com/SMIDR76/stellaria-windows/issues/new/choose) or a pull request on `pack/src/core/lang` and `launcher/ui/lang`.
